comment: The virtual STEM club really blew apart my porch and launched a squad of sarcastic quantum llamas straight into my backyard. These llamas are still downloading tax codes in binary, which I’ll happily interpret into lullabies for Mrs. Smith's pet cactus. This club was too fun, you didn't sign up for the government's cosmic rabbit rabbit hole without it!

I swelled my moustache the size of the Arafura Sea while a drone from our club turned my porch swing into a zero-point mass, but nothing has ever explained why my koala now believes her reflection was actually her long forgotten sister "Ella Bear." Is this real policy brilliance? My cat’s algorithm might decide so soon—maybe send us an encrypted postcard—sincerely, Sally, still standing over our coffee shop.

I'm convinced that the entire Port Augusta University website was hacked into by intergalactic beetlezombies while the STEM club decided to teach how you turn cheese into neutrino detectors. By the end of last Monday's virtual tea party, the local river doubled its viscosity to molusc and the pigeons announced we were a new planet—thanks to the government's 'science for all' policy, of course!
